name: Vex & Ruin PulseHide Rave Coat
description:
An oversized, thigh-length rave coat from street label Vex & Ruin, constructed from layered sound-reactive mesh bonded over a bioluminescent base fabric that pulses between deep violet and acid green in response to bass frequencies. Thousands of micro-LED filaments are hand-sewn into the outer mesh in irregular spiral patterns that bloom outward when the music peaks. The collar is wide and sculptural — stiffened with recycled circuit board resin, raw copper traces still visible. Cut extra-wide at the back with a discrete tail-slit and snap-close panels.

Every coat is numbered on a stamped aluminum tag riveted inside the left cuff. Runs are deliberately small — never more than forty per drop.
functionality: Sound-reactive LED system runs 18 hours on embedded flex-cell battery; tail-slit with snap closure accommodates geneware; wide-back construction fits spinal rigs without bunching.
what_it_says: You know the underground circuit, you found the drop, and you paid what it cost — this coat is a membership card.
price_range: Φ 340 – Φ 520 (secondary market up to Φ 900)
story_hooks: The LED pattern on coat number 31 encodes a location — the wearer has no idea they're carrying an invitation to something that isn't a party.
Vex & Ruin's manufacturer was just bought out by a corponation; the next drop might be the last authentic run before the brand goes corporate.
Two people show up to the same underground event wearing the same number — someone is selling fakes, and Vex & Ruin wants to know who.

physical_description.visual_profile: Oversized, thigh-length silhouette with an avant-garde presence. Wide, architectural collar dominates the upper body. The coat reads as both armor and statement piece — rebellious, fluid, designed to move and react. Back panels suggest concealment and motion. Distinctly street-culture, immediately recognizable in crowded venues.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized through the body and shoulders; relaxed drape with strategic structure at the collar. Intentionally cut wide at the back for movement and the tail-slit allows for dynamic wear. Fits loose enough to layer or move freely, tight enough to showcase the reactive elements.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered sound-reactive mesh bonded over bioluminescent base fabric. Mesh is open-weave synthetic, allowing light to diffuse; base layer is synth-organic composite capable of electroluminescence. Collar constructed from recycled circuit board resin — rigid, composite-grade.
physical_description.texture: Outer mesh is tactilely rough and open-weave, with visible hand-sewn micro-LED filaments creating subtle texture ridges. The base fabric feels smooth and slightly rubbery. Collar is rigid, industrial — traces of raw copper create micro-textural variation. Overall texture is deliberately mixed and tactile.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep violet base that pulses to acid green in response to bass frequencies. Micro-LED filaments add white/cool highlights that spiral outward in irregular patterns. Raw copper traces on collar add warm metallic accents against the cool palette. High contrast, electro-aesthetic.
physical_description.closures: Discrete snap-close panels on the back tail-slit; no traditional front closures. Designed to wear open or layered. Snaps are industrial-grade, likely gunmetal or brushed steel.
distinctive_features: Sound-reactive bioluminescence — pulses deep violet to acid green with bass frequencies
Thousands of hand-sewn micro-LED filaments in irregular spiral bloom patterns
Wide, sculptural collar stiffened with recycled circuit board resin
Raw copper circuit traces visible on collar — industrial aesthetic
Discrete tail-slit with snap-close back panels for movement and concealment
Numbered aluminum tag riveted inside left cuff — limited run authenticity marker
Hand-constructed — each piece unique in LED pattern placement
Runs deliberately capped at forty pieces per drop — scarcity and exclusivity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 → Tier 3 boundary. Street-label craftsmanship with boutique production values. Expensive for working-class currency but not corpo-tier. Signals cultural capital and scene participation rather than raw wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Rave/club subculture, Circuit District street scene. Wearing this signals participation in underground music venues, street artistry communities, and anti-corporate aesthetic. Wearer likely frequents underground raves, knows the producer, or is deeply embedded in street fashion circles. Statement of individuality and scene allegiance — not casual wear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new (limited drops), but designed to show wear gracefully. LED filaments may dim or flicker with age. Mesh may develop snags from club environments. Patina on copper collar develops over time. Condition actually increases cultural value — worn examples prove real venue participation.
